learningObjectives.title: The consequences of a sedentary lifestyle

questions.q: According to the World Health Organisation, health is best defined as which of the following?
options: A state of complete physical, emotional and social wellbeing, and not merely the absence of disease
The ability to carry out everyday activities without getting tired
Being physically fit and free from all injury
Having no illness, disease or infirmity of any kind
questions.explain: The WHO definition covers physical, emotional and social wellbeing, not simply the absence of illness.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an emotional (mental) health benefit of taking part in physical activity?
options: Reduced stress and improved ability to control emotions
Making new friends through a team
questions.explain: Emotional health benefits include reducing stress and better management of emotions and self-esteem.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates a social health benefit of sport?
options: Making new friends and cooperating with others
Reducing the risk of heart disease
questions.explain: Social health involves meeting people, making friends and cooperating with others.

questions.q: What is meant by a sedentary lifestyle?
options: A lifestyle with irregular or no physical activity
A lifestyle involving daily vigorous training
A diet that is high in carbohydrates
A lifestyle with a balanced diet and moderate exercise
questions.explain: A sedentary lifestyle is one that involves little, irregular or no physical activity.

questions.q: Which macronutrient is the body's main source of energy for exercise?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates are the body's primary and preferred source of energy, especially for higher-intensity work.

questions.q: Which nutrient is mainly used for the growth and repair of muscles and body tissue?
questions.explain: Protein is essential for the growth and repair of muscle and tissue.

questions.q: Which mineral is particularly important for maintaining strong bones and teeth?
questions.explain: Calcium is a mineral that helps keep bones and teeth strong and healthy.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a physical health benefit of regular exercise?
options: Making new friends through a club
Reducing the risk of coronary heart disease
Helping to maintain a healthy body weight
questions.explain: Making friends is a social benefit; the others are physical health benefits.

questions.q: Why does taking part in exercise tend to improve a person's emotional health?
options: It releases endorphins/serotonin that reduce stress and improve mood
It increases the amount of fat stored in the body
It slows down the digestive system
It reduces the amount of oxygen carried in the blood
questions.explain: Exercise triggers the release of feel-good hormones such as serotonin/endorphins, reducing stress.

questions.q: Which of the following is a likely consequence of a sedentary lifestyle?
options: Increased risk of coronary heart disease
questions.explain: Inactivity raises the risk of coronary heart disease alongside obesity, hypertension and type 2 diabetes.

questions.q: Vitamins and minerals are together classed as which type of nutrient?
questions.explain: Vitamins and minerals are micronutrients, needed in small amounts to maintain health.

questions.q: What is the main function of fibre in a performer's diet?
options: It aids digestion and helps the digestive system work properly
It is the body's main energy source
It is used to build and repair muscle
It carries oxygen around the body
questions.explain: Fibre supports healthy digestion and can help slow the release of energy.

questions.q: What is one effect of dehydration on a performer during exercise?
options: The blood becomes thicker, so the heart has to work harder
Muscles grow and repair more quickly
questions.explain: Dehydration makes the blood more viscous, raising heart rate and reducing performance.

questions.q: Why is the mineral iron important for a performer?
options: It helps form haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood
It builds strong bones and teeth
It is the main energy source for sprinting
It insulates the body against the cold
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, which transports oxygen to the working muscles.

questions.q: In the days before a marathon, a runner greatly increases their intake of pasta and other carbohydrates to maximise energy stores. What is this strategy called?
questions.explain: Endurance athletes use carbohydrate loading to maximise glycogen stores before a long event.

questions.q: An office worker drives everywhere, sits at a desk all day, watches television all evening and eats a high-calorie diet. Which condition is he most at risk of developing?
questions.explain: Combining inactivity with excess calorie intake increases the risk of obesity and type 2 diabetes.

questions.q: A teenager joins a football team and reports feeling less stressed and more confident, as well as having made several new friends. Which aspects of health has this improved?
questions.explain: Reduced stress and greater confidence are emotional benefits, while making friends is a social benefit.

questions.q: A weightlifter wants to increase muscle mass and repair muscle after heavy training. Which nutrient should they make sure they eat enough of?
questions.explain: Protein supports the growth and repair of muscle, which is key for strength and power athletes.

questions.q: Which statement best describes obesity?
options: Having an excessive amount of body fat that may negatively affect health
Being slightly above your recommended training weight
Having a low level of muscular strength
Eating a diet that is too high in protein
questions.explain: Obesity is a condition of having excess body fat that can harm health and performance.

questions.q: During long, low-intensity aerobic exercise such as a slow steady run, which nutrient becomes an important source of energy?
questions.explain: Fat is a key energy source for prolonged, low-intensity aerobic activity.
